summary: In the non-shielded vdW branch the derivative term is multiplied by rij instead of divided by it, giving a vdW force wrong by a factor r^2 for force fields with vdw_type == 2.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1256-1260 (analytic kernel, 'else' == no shielding): 'exp2 = exp(0.5*alpha*(1.0-rij/r_vdw)); exp1 = exp2*exp2; etmp = epsilon*(exp1-2.0*exp2); evdwl = Tap*etmp; fvdwl = dTap*etmp-Tap*epsilon*(alpha/r_vdw)*(exp1-exp2)*rij;'.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:164-165 has 'CEvd = dTap * e_vdW - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;' and the table generator inside this same KOKKOS file, PairReaxFFKokkos::LR_vdW_Coulomb (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:669-670), also divides: 'lr->CEvd = dTap * twbp->D * (exp1 - 2.0 * exp2) - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;'.  Note dTap here is already dTap/dr divided by r (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1228-1233 adds d_tap[1]/rij), so the second term must carry the same 1/r.
failure_scenario: Any ReaxFF force field whose ffield header sets vdW type 2 (inner wall, no shielding) run with pair_style reaxff/kk and control->tabulate == 0: the vdW force term is scaled by r^2 instead of 1/r (a factor r^2 at r~3 A is ~10x too large and of the wrong r-dependence), so trajectories, forces and pressure differ from pair_style reaxff; energies stay correct, which makes it hard to notice.
suggested_fix: Change '*rij' to '/rij' at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1260 to match reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:165.

summary: TagPairReaxZero unconditionally writes d_hb_num(n), but that view is only allocated when cut_hbsq > 0, so a run with hbond_cutoff 0 dereferences a null view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1592-1599 'void PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagPairReaxZero, const int &n) const { d_total_bo(n) = 0; d_CdDelta(n) = 0; d_bo_num(n) = 0; d_hb_num(n) = 0; ... }' - no guard.  allocate_array() only creates it conditionally: ':1530-1533 if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) { MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_num,"reaxff/kk:hb_num",nmax); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_list,...); }'.  Every other use is guarded (:1629, :1764, :1851, :1900, :3327 behind 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0)' at :1024).  cut_hbsq is set from the control file at :360 'cut_hbsq = api->control->hbond_cut * api->control->hbond_cut;' and the CPU style explicitly supports hbond_cut == 0 (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:133, reaxff_forces.cpp:51, reaxff_init_md.cpp:56 all test 'if (control->hbond_cut > 0)').
failure_scenario: A control file containing 'hbond_cutoff 0.0' (the documented way to switch H-bonds off) with pair_style reaxff/kk -> d_hb_num is a default-constructed View whose data pointer is null -> segfault (host) or illegal memory access (GPU) in the very first TagPairReaxZero launch.
suggested_fix: Guard the write: 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) d_hb_num(n) = 0;' (or always allocate d_hb_num with size nmax).

summary: thb_cutsq is hardcoded to 1e-5 instead of taken from api->control->thb_cutsq, so the control-file keyword 'thb_cutoff_sq' is silently ignored by reaxff/kk.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:365-366 'thb_cut = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cut); thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.000010); //thb_cut*thb_cut;'.  src/REAXFF/reaxff_control.cpp:101-102 reads it from the control file ('} else if (keyword == "thb_cutoff_sq") { control->thb_cutsq = values.next_double();') and the CPU kernel uses it: src/REAXFF/reaxff_valence_angles.cpp:222 '(bo_ij->BO * bo_jk->BO > control->thb_cutsq)'.  The KOKKOS angular screening uses the hardcoded value at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2574 'if (bo_ij <= thb_cut || bo_ik <= thb_cut || bo_ij * bo_ik <= thb_cutsq) continue;'.
failure_scenario: A control file with a non-default 'thb_cutoff_sq' (e.g. 0.001 to speed up the valence-angle loop): pair_style reaxff uses it, pair_style reaxff/kk keeps 1e-5, so the two include different sets of valence angles and give different energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Set thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cutsq); in setup().

summary: TagPairReaxFindBondSpecies writes d_tmpid/d_tmpbo before checking the MAXSPECBOND bound and keeps writing past the end of the row for every further bond, since the error is only reported after the whole kernel finishes.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4400-4407 'if (bo_tmp >= 0.10) { d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; d_tmpbo(i,nj) = bo_tmp; nj++; if (nj > MAXSPECBOND) k_error_flag.view<DeviceType>()() = 1; }' - the views are created with second extent MAXSPECBOND (:4350-4351 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_tmpid,tmpid,nmax,MAXSPECBOND,...)'), so index nj == MAXSPECBOND is already out of range and the guard fires only afterwards.  The error is not acted on until FindBondSpecies() returns (:4374-4375).  The CPU base has the same off-by-one (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:786-791) but calls error->all() immediately, so at most one element is overwritten there.
failure_scenario: With 'fix reaxff/species' on a structure where some atom has 25 or more bonds with BO >= 0.10 (MAXSPECBOND is 24, reaxff_defs.h:54): the kernel writes d_tmpid(i,24), d_tmpid(i,25), ... , silently corrupting the next atoms' rows (and running past the allocation for the last atom) before the run is finally aborted with 'Increase MAXSPECBOND'.
suggested_fix: Test the bound before writing: 'if (nj >= MAXSPECBOND) { k_error_flag...() = 1; break; } d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; ...'.

summary: PairReaxFFKokkos::Init_Lookup_Tables() builds the spline tables for every LAMMPS type pair without checking map[i] == -1, so an unmapped (NULL) type indexes reax_param.tbp[-1]; Deallocate_Lookup_Tables() conversely skips those pairs and leaks their arrays.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:509-531 'for (i = 1; i <= num_atom_types; ++i) { for (j = i; j <= num_atom_types; ++j) { ... LR_vdW_Coulomb(i, j, r * dr, &(LR[i][j].y[r])); ...' - no 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;', while LR_vdW_Coulomb dereferences ':626 twbp = &(api->system->reax_param.tbp[map[i]][map[j]]);'.  Both the init_md() copy loop (:426-429 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;') and Deallocate_Lookup_Tables (:591 'if ((map[i] == -1) || (map[j] == -1)) continue;') do guard on map.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_lookup.cpp:195-198 restricts the loops to types actually present ('if (aggregated[i])') and sets LR[i][j].n = 0 otherwise (:255).
failure_scenario: 'pair_coeff * * ffield.reax NULL C H' (a NULL type, common with hybrid or with fixed/wall particles) plus 'tabulate' enabled in the control file -> tbp[-1][...] is read out of bounds inside LR_vdW_Coulomb -> garbage table values or a segfault; even without a crash the six spline arrays of every unmapped pair are never freed.
suggested_fix: Skip unmapped types in Init_Lookup_Tables (set LR[i][j].n = 0 for them) and drop the map[] guard from Deallocate_Lookup_Tables so that whatever was allocated is freed.

summary: TagPairReaxBondOrder2 writes d_CdDelta[j] for its neighbours j, which is a redundant benign data race with the thread that owns atom j (and with the already-executed zeroing kernel).
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2205-2211 'd_Cdbo(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi2(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_CdDelta[j] = 0.0; } d_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;' - d_CdDelta[j] belongs to another thread's atom.  d_CdDelta was already zeroed for all nmax entries by TagPairReaxZero (:1594 'd_CdDelta(n) = 0;') which runs earlier in compute() (:855).
failure_scenario: Both threads store 0.0 so the value is correct, but it is a concurrent unsynchronised write that thread sanitizers and Kokkos debug tooling flag, and it hides the fact that the write is dead.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'd_CdDelta[j] = 0.0;' (and the redundant 'd_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;') lines - TagPairReaxZero already covers them.

summary: v_tally3_atom() is dead code that would race if it were ever used, because it writes d_vatom directly instead of through the scatter/atomic view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4026-4050 defines PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::v_tally3_atom(...) with ':4047-4049 if (vflag_atom) { for (int n = 0; n < 6; n++) d_vatom(i,n) += v[n]; }' - a plain non-atomic read-modify-write, unlike v_tally/v_tally3/v_tally4 which all go through ScatterViewHelper (:3934-3935, :3952-3953, :4013-4014).  grep over the file shows no call site (the only occurrences are the declaration pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:437 and this definition).
failure_scenario: No effect today; if anyone wires it up, per-atom virials would be silently corrupted under HALFTHREAD/GPU.
suggested_fix: Remove v_tally3_atom (declaration and definition), or convert it to the ScatterView pattern and template it on NEIGHFLAG like the other tally helpers.

summary: Inner loop counters shadow the pack-decoded atom indices j and k in ComputeAngularPreprocessed, making the kernel very easy to break.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2740-2741 'const int j = pack.i1; const int k = pack.i2;' then :2769 'for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) fitmp[j] = 0.0;' and :2783 'for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) fjtmp[k] = 0.0;'.  The loop variables shadow the atom indices; the code is correct only because the uses at :2771-2773 and :2785-2787 are outside the loop scope.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers today, but any edit that moves a use of j or k inside one of those loops silently reads a component index instead of an atom index.
suggested_fix: Rename the loop counters (e.g. 'for (int d = 0; d < 3; d++)') as the rest of the kernel does.

summary: compute() reuses a single EV_FLOAT_REAX 'ev' across all kernel dispatches and unconditionally does 'ev_all += ev' after each section, so a section that ran parallel_for (no reduction) adds the previous section's reduction result a second time.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:775 'EV_FLOAT_REAX ev; EV_FLOAT_REAX ev_all;' then :918-932 'if (eflag_either) parallel_reduce(...ComputeBond1<HALF,1>...,*this,ev); else parallel_for(...ComputeBond1<HALF,0>...,*this); ev_all += ev;' - in the else branch ev still holds the LJ/Coulomb reduction from :809-816.  The same shape appears at :941/:948 (Multi2, guarded by eflag_either), :992/:998, :1011/:1017, :1030/:1036 (guarded by evflag) and :1056/:1065 (Bond2, guarded by vflag_either).
failure_scenario: Benign today only because the custom ev_setup (:4100-4105) forces vflag_global = 0 for the VIRIAL_FDOTR path that reaxff always takes, so ev.v[] is never filled, and evdwl/ecoul are guarded by eflag_global which implies eflag_either.  Any future change that writes ev.evdwl/ev.ecoul/ev.v in ComputeHydrogen, ComputeTorsion or ComputeLJCoulomb outside those guards silently double counts the energy or virial.
suggested_fix: Reset ev (ev = EV_FLOAT_REAX();) before each section, or move 'ev_all += ev;' inside the reduction branch.

summary: The neighbor-index blocking buffer stores the neighbor index in an unsigned short, truncating for atoms with more than 65535 neighbours in the nonbonded list.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:118 'using blocking_t = unsigned short int;'; pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1633 'blocking_t selected_jj[blocksize];' and :1653 'selected_jj[nnz] = jj_current;' where jj_current runs to jnum-1 = d_numneigh[i]-1 (:1621).  Same at :1768/:1789.
failure_scenario: A very large nonb_cut or a pathologically dense system giving an atom >65535 entries in its half neighbor list: the stored index wraps and the wrong neighbor is used for the bond-order list, producing wrong bonds and forces with no diagnostic.
suggested_fix: Use int for selected_jj, or add a check that d_numneigh[i] fits in blocking_t.

summary: TagPairReaxZero writes d_hb_num(n) unconditionally, but that view is allocated only when cut_hbsq > 0. A control file with 'hbond_cutoff 0.0' - the documented way to switch H-bonds off - leaves it default-constructed, so the first kernel launch writes through a null data pointer.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1596 unguarded vs the conditional allocation at :1530-1533; every other use of d_hb_num in the file sits behind a 'cut_hbsq > 0.0' test).

summary: pair gran/hooke/history/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently diverging from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:350 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' (imass/jmass are plain rmass, lines 274 and 306). CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:133-142 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);' plus the mass_rigid refresh/forward comm at pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:25-41. 'grep -n fix_rigid src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' finds nothing, and the /kk init_style (line 63-93) adds no guard.
failure_scenario: Granular input combining 'fix rigid' with 'pair_style gran/hooke/history/kk' -> the normal damping and Coulomb friction cap use the single-particle mass rather than the body mass, giving silently different forces than the identical non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Port the mass_rigid array to a device DualView (filled from fix_rigid->extract plus a forward comm each reneighbor) or error out in init_style when fix_rigid is set.

summary: gran/hooke/history/kk stores special_bonds lj factors in the base class int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0/1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:142-145 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' with src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];' -- the /kk header (src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h:66-104) declares no KK_FLOAT special_lj shadow, unlike the other KOKKOS pair styles (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lennard_mdf_kokkos.h:89). Kernel use: line 297 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);' and line 300 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. CPU: src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:53 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'.
failure_scenario: 'special_bonds lj 0.5 1 1' with gran/hooke/history/kk: 1-2 contacts are dropped entirely (0.5 truncates to 0) instead of being scaled by 0.5, changing forces and the stored shear history.
suggested_fix: Add 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' to the three KOKKOS granular pair style headers so the double factors survive, or widen Pair::special_lj to double.

summary: d_neighbors_touch / d_numneigh_touch are allocated every time the neighbor list is resized but are never read or written anywhere, wasting a full neighbor-list-sized device allocation.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:160-164 'if (d_numneigh.extent(0) != d_numneigh_touch.extent(0)) d_numneigh_touch = typename AT::t_int_1d(...); if (d_neighbors.extent(0) != d_neighbors_touch.extent(0) || ...) d_neighbors_touch = typename AT::t_neighbors_2d("pair:neighbors_touch",d_neighbors.extent(0),d_neighbors.extent(1));'. Declared at src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h:90-91. 'grep -rn "d_neighbors_touch|d_numneigh_touch" src/KOKKOS/*' matches only those declaration and allocation lines (and the identical block in pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:160-164) -- no kernel ever touches them. t_neighbors_2d is tdual_int_2d_dl (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1282-1283), so the allocation duplicates the entire int neighbor list.
failure_scenario: Any gran/hooke/history/kk or gran/hertz/history/kk run allocates a second array of nmax*maxneighs ints on the GPU that is never used; on a large granular run this can be hundreds of MB of wasted device memory and can trigger an out-of-memory abort.
suggested_fix: Delete the two members and their allocation block from both granular history KOKKOS pair styles.

summary: The kernel writes the device side of FixNeighHistoryKokkos::k_firstflag/k_firstvalue but never calls modify<DeviceType>() on those DualViews.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:166-172 syncs and takes views ('fix_historyKK->k_firstflag.template sync<DeviceType>(); ... Kokkos::deep_copy(d_firsttouch,0);') and the kernel then writes them (lines 313-315 'd_firstshear(i,3*jj) = 0;', line 319 'd_firsttouch(i,jj) = 1;', lines 415-417). No 'k_firstflag.modify<DeviceType>()' / 'k_firstvalue.modify<DeviceType>()' appears afterwards, unlike src/KOKKOS/fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:237-238 which does exactly that after its own kernel. Same omission in pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:166-172.
failure_scenario: Currently masked because post_neighbor() leaves the DualView marked device-modified, so subsequent sync<Device> calls are no-ops; but any future host-side write or sync_host() of the history arrays between two pair computes would silently discard the shear history updated on device.
suggested_fix: Add 'fix_historyKK->k_firstflag.template modify<DeviceType>(); fix_historyKK->k_firstvalue.template modify<DeviceType>();' after the parallel_for in both granular history KOKKOS pair styles.

summary: The improper cvff/kk device kernel reads the host-only raw pointer `sign[type]` instead of the device view `d_sign[type]`, so on a GPU build it dereferences a host address inside the kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:278 (inside operator()(TagImproperCvffCompute...) which is KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION): `if (sign[type] == -1) {` / `p = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0) - p;` / `pd = -pd;`. `sign` is the base class member `int *sign, *multiplicity;` (src/MOLECULE/improper_cvff.h:40) allocated with memory->create in ImproperCvff::allocate. The Kokkos mirror exists and is kept in sync but is never used: `DAT::tdual_int_1d k_sign,k_multiplicity;` / `typename AT::t_int_1d d_sign,d_multiplicity;` (src/KOKKOS/improper_cvff_kokkos.h:88,91), filled in coeff()/read_restart() (improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:388,393,409,414), allocated in allocate() (:366,370) and synced at :92 `k_sign.template sync<DeviceType>();`. Two lines above, the sibling array IS read correctly through its device view: `const int m = d_multiplicity[type];` (:247).
failure_scenario: Any GPU (CUDA/HIP/SYCL, non-UVM) run with `improper_style cvff/kk`: the kernel dereferences a host pointer -> illegal memory access / crash, or silently garbage `sign` values and therefore wrong improper energies and forces for `sign = -1` types. CPU-only Kokkos builds are unaffected, which is why it can pass CI.
suggested_fix: Replace `sign[type]` with `d_sign[type]` in the kernel (matching the `d_multiplicity[type]` usage on line 247).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 17)
summary: The improper cvff/kk device kernel reads the host-only base-class pointer sign[type] instead of the device view d_sign[type] (which is allocated, filled and synced but never used), so on a GPU it dereferences a host address inside the kernel.
evidence: improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:278 'if (sign[type] == -1)' inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION operator(); line 247 correctly uses d_multiplicity[type]; k_sign synced at :92.
failure_scenario: improper_style cvff/kk on CUDA/HIP: illegal memory access, or garbage sign -> wrong improper energies/forces for sign=-1 types. CPU-only Kokkos builds hide it.
suggested_fix: Use d_sign[type].

summary: FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() drops the base class's 'if (filename == "NULL") return;' early exit, so 'fix ... reaxff/bonds/kk N NULL' creates and writes a file literally named NULL instead of suppressing file output.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/bonds/kk 10 NULL  (the documented way to enable dump-image bond rendering without a bonds file) -> rank 0 creates a file named 'NULL' in the working directory and writes a full bond table into it every 10 steps.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (filename == "NULL") return;' right after the FindBond_kokkos() call, matching FixReaxFFBonds::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds().

summary: fix reaxff/bonds/kk never fills numobjs/numneigh/neighid, so the inherited FixReaxFFBonds::image() always returns 0 and dump image silently renders no ReaxFF bonds.
evidence: src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:377-383: 'int FixReaxFFBonds::image(int *&objs, double **&parms) { ... if (!numobjs) return 0;' and the body reads 'numneigh[i]' / 'neighid[i][jj]'. numobjs is set only in FixReaxFFBonds::FindBond() (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:187 'numobjs = 0;' and :206 'numobjs += nj;'). FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() (src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.cpp:102-137) calls PairReaxFFKokkos::FindBond_kokkos() instead, which fills only device views in the pair style and never touches numobjs/numneigh/neighid; FixReaxFFBondsKokkos does not override image().
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/bonds/kk 10 NULL  +  dump  d all image ... bonds fix 1 ...  -> the images contain the atoms but no bonds, with no error message; the same input with the non-kk fix draws them.
suggested_fix: Either override image() in FixReaxFFBondsKokkos to build the object list from the pair style's device bond data (syncing it to the host first), or make init() refuse the combination with a clear error when the fix is used as a dump image bond source.

summary: fix reaxff/bonds/kk inherits FixReaxFFBonds::allocate(), so numneigh/neighid/abo (nmax x MAXREAXBOND) are allocated and grown but never used by the KOKKOS path, and memory_usage() no longer reports them.
evidence: src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:68 'allocate();' in the base constructor allocates 'numneigh' (nmax), 'neighid' (nmax x MAXREAXBOND, tagint) and 'abo' (nmax x MAXREAXBOND, double); allocate() is not virtual (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.h:49 'void allocate();') and FixReaxFFBondsKokkos does not override it. src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.cpp:141-152: 'double FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::memory_usage() { bytes = nbuf*sizeof(double); // These are accounted for in PairReaxFFKokkos: //bytes += nmax*sizeof(int); ...' -- the commented-out terms are exactly the arrays the base fix (not the pair style) still owns.
failure_scenario: A 1M-atom reaxff/kk run with fix reaxff/bonds/kk wastes ~1M*MAXREAXBOND*(sizeof(tagint)+sizeof(double)) bytes of host memory that no code reads, and 'info memory' under-reports the fix's footprint.
suggested_fix: Make FixReaxFFBonds::allocate()/destroy() virtual and override them in the KOKKOS class to be no-ops (or keep them and restore the memory_usage terms).

summary: TuneKokkos opens its log file only on rank 0 and calls the collective error->all() inside that rank-0-only branch, so a failure to open the file makes rank 0 abort collectively while every other rank continues, i.e. a hang or an MPI abort mismatch in parallel runs; the file is also handled with raw fopen/fclose instead of SafeFilePtr.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:96-104: 'if (comm->me == 0) { std::string filename = fmt::format("tuning-{}.log", my_name); tuning_logfile = fopen(filename.c_str(),"w"); if (tuning_logfile == nullptr) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot open tuning logfile {}: {}", ...); } else { tuning_logfile = nullptr; }'. Project rules: error->all() only when all ranks hit the error, error->one() for a single rank; prefer SafeFilePtr for FILE* resources.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank KOKKOS run with 'package kokkos ... tune' in a read-only working directory: rank 0 enters Error::all (MPI_Barrier/abort protocol), the other ranks proceed to allocate() and into the run -> deadlock or an unclean abort instead of the intended error message.
suggested_fix: Use error->one() for the rank-0 failure (or broadcast the failure flag and call error->all on every rank), and hold the FILE* in a SafeFilePtr.

summary: get_optimal_combination_idx() seeds opt_perf with the raw sample performance[0][0] instead of the representative value of combination 0, so in AVERAGE/MEDIAN mode opt_perf can be a single outlier sample that no combination's representative value beats; the returned index is then 0 with an inflated opt_perf, and regular_performance_check() later measures every real performance against it and can trigger spurious re-scans.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:465-466 'opt_perf = performance[0][0]; int opt_idx = 0;' followed by the loop computing p_i (max/average/median per combination) and 'if (p_i > opt_perf) { opt_perf = p_i; opt_idx = i; }' (496-499). With mode AVERAGE_VALUE or MEDIAN_VALUE, p_0 <= max sample of row 0, so a large performance[0][0] is never replaced. regular_performance_check(): 'diff = (opt_perf - perf)/opt_perf; if (diff > relative_tolerance) ... re-scan' (543-573).
failure_scenario: tune mode 'average' or 'median' with a noisy first sample of the first combination (e.g. a step right after setup): opt_perf is the outlier, every later check reports the performance as degraded, and the tuner keeps re-scanning instead of settling.
suggested_fix: Initialize opt_perf to the representative value of combination 0 (compute p_0 first) or to -1.0 so the loop always assigns it.

summary: UPSTREAM CPU DEFECT, faithfully mirrored by the KOKKOS port. The pair force is formed as 'forcelj * rshift / r' where the analytic gradient of the tallied energy requires 'forcelj / rshift / r', so every force is off by a factor rshift^2 and does not match the energy. The sibling style lj/expand gets it right.
verified_by: orchestrator. With lj1=48*eps*sigma^12, lj2=24*eps*sigma^6 (pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:266-267) and r6inv=1/rshift^6, forcelj = -rshift*dE/drshift, so the scalar multiplying del must be forcelj/(rshift*r). src/pair_lj_expand.cpp:115 and :409 use exactly 'forcelj / rshift / r' for the identical energy form, while src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:122 (compute) and :396 (single) use 'forcelj * rshift / r'. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_sphere_kokkos.cpp:154 copies the base, and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_kokkos.cpp:158 copies the correct one. NOTE: the force-style YAML fixtures for lj/expand/sphere were generated from the current code and must be regenerated with the fix.

summary: compute() copies FixStoreAtom's initial positions for every local+ghost atom through a scalar host loop and a full host-to-device transfer on EVERY timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:100-109 'const int n_sync = atom->nlocal + atom->nghost; auto h_x0 = k_x0.view_host(); for (int i = 0; i < n_sync; i++) { h_x0(i,0) = ...; } k_x0.modify_host(); k_x0.template sync<DeviceType>();' - unconditional, executed once per compute() call.
failure_scenario: Any GPU run with 'bond_style harmonic/restrain/kk': every MD step pays an O(nlocal+nghost) host loop plus a 3*(nlocal+nghost)*sizeof(KK_FLOAT) H2D transfer, which is the same order as the x/f transfer the KOKKOS package exists to avoid; the /kk variant can easily be slower than the plain CPU style.
suggested_fix: Refresh k_x0 only when the atom set changed (neighbor->ago == 0 or a stored update->ntimestep guard), or better, store the initial positions in a device DualView owned by the style and update it in the exchange/border callbacks.

summary: The device minimum_image() applies at most ONE periodic wrap per dimension (if) where Domain::minimum_image loops (while), and it silently drops the 'atoms have moved too far apart' error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:245-263 'if (xperiodic) { if (Kokkos::abs(dx) > xprd_half) { if (dx < 0.0) dx += xprd; else dx -= xprd; } }' (and the same single-if for y, z and for all three triclinic branches at :264-295). CPU src/domain.cpp:1219-1248 and 1250-1290 use 'while (fabs(dx) > xprd_half) {...}' plus 'if (fabs(dx) > (MAXIMGCOUNT * xprd)) error->one(file,line,"Atoms have moved too far apart ({}) for minimum image");'. The CPU base src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_harmonic_restrain.cpp:78 calls exactly that: 'domain->minimum_image(FLERR, delx, dely, delz);'.
failure_scenario: Stored initial positions that are more than 1.5 box lengths apart (box shrunk by fix deform/npt after init_style stored x0, or unwrapped x0 for a stretched molecule) leave a residual image after one wrap, so the reference length r0 - and hence the restraint force - differs from the CPU style; the triclinic branch can also need a second y wrap after the z tilt shift.
suggested_fix: Change each 'if (Kokkos::abs(d?) > ?prd_half)' into a 'while' loop, matching Domain::minimum_image, and optionally set an error flag when the displacement exceeds MAXIMGCOUNT box lengths.

summary: The GPU team kernels stage atom tags through a double shared-memory buffer, so tagint values lose precision in LAMMPS_BIGBIG builds and the newton/triclinic (itag+jtag)%2 tie-break can pick the wrong owner.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:665 'other_x[MY_II + 4 * atoms_per_bin] = itag;' and :779 'const tagint jtag = other_x[m + 4 * atoms_per_bin];' (same pattern at :1389/:1507 in build_ItemSizeGPU), where other_x is 'double* other_x' (:634, :1354).  The flat kernel reads the tags exactly: :532 'const tagint jtag = tag(j);'.  With -DLAMMPS_BIGBIG tagint is int64_t (src/lmptype.h) and values above 2^53 are not representable in a double.
failure_scenario: A LAMMPS_BIGBIG run with atom IDs above 2^53 rounds jtag, so 'if (itag > jtag)' and the '(itag+jtag) % 2' parity test can differ between the two owners of an owned/ghost pair -> the pair is either stored twice or not at all in a half/newton/triclinic list.
suggested_fix: Store tags in a separate tagint-typed slice of the shared-memory block (or read tag(j) directly in the tie-break) instead of round-tripping them through double.

summary: The team kernels return from a subset of the block when mbins is not a multiple of BINS_PER_TEAM, so the later __syncthreads_count()/team_barrier() calls are reached by only part of the block.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:630-632 'const int ibin = dev.league_rank()*BINS_PER_TEAM+MY_BIN; if (ibin >= mbins) return;' where MY_BIN = dev.team_rank()/atoms_per_bin varies within the team (BINS_PER_TEAM == factor == 2 whenever atoms_per_bin < 64, see :264).  The block-wide synchronizations at :671 'int test = (__syncthreads_count(i >= 0 && i < nlocal) == 0);' and :737/:760/:833 'dev.team_barrier();' are then executed by only the MY_BIN==0 half of the block.  Same shape at :992 and :1352.
failure_scenario: An odd mbins with atoms_per_bin < 64 leaves the MY_BIN==1 threads exited before the barriers; the collective is formally undefined and __syncthreads_count returns a partial count, which can make the surviving threads take the early-return branch and skip building neighbor lists for that bin.
suggested_fix: Replace the early return with a predicate that keeps all threads participating in the barriers (e.g. set a local 'valid' flag and guard the body with it), or size the league so every team's bins are in range.

summary: DomainKokkos declares 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;' which is never defined anywhere and hides the three Domain::closest_image() overloads for anyone holding a DomainKokkos*.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.h:50: 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;'.  'grep -rn "DomainKokkos::closest_image" src' finds no definition; src/domain.h:143-145 declares the three non-virtual base overloads 'int closest_image(int, int); int closest_image(const double *const, int); void closest_image(const double *const, const double *const, double *const);' which name lookup in DomainKokkos would hide.  The KOKKOS callers (fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:1031, fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2388, neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp) each define their own closest_image member instead.
failure_scenario: Any new code that calls domain->closest_image(...) through a DomainKokkos pointer gets either an undefined-symbol link error (two-int form) or a compile error (the other overloads are hidden).
suggested_fix: Delete the declaration, or implement it and mark it as an explicit using-declaration of the base overloads.

summary: FixEnforce2DKokkos::setup() unconditionally calls post_force(), dropping the base class's rRESPA branch that zeroes the z force in every stored respa level array, and the style never rejects rRESPA the way its sibling /kk fixes do.
failure_scenario: CPU-only KOKKOS build, `-sf kk`, `run_style respa` with `fix enforce2d`: at setup the per-level force arrays keep whatever f_z they were given (e.g. from a fix langevin or an added force in an inner level), because the level loop that the CPU fix runs is skipped; Respa::sum_flevel_f then re-injects that z component on the first step of a 2d run.
suggested_fix: Either drop the setup() override so the base class version runs (post_force is virtual and will still dispatch to the KOKKOS kernel), or add an init() override that rejects rRESPA like the neighbouring /kk fixes do.

summary: PairHybridOverlayKokkos::coeff is a stale copy of PairHybridOverlay::coeff and still carries the old, less specific error message for an unknown sub-style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_overlay_kokkos.cpp:61-64 'if (m == nstyles) { if (strcmp(arg[2],"none") == 0) none = 1; else error->all(FLERR,"Pair coeff for hybrid has invalid style: {}", arg[2]); }' vs src/pair_hybrid_overlay.cpp:62-65 'if (strcmp(arg[2],"none") == 0) none = 1; else error->all(FLERR,"Expected hybrid sub-style instead of {} in pair_coeff command", arg[2]);'. A diff of the two coeff() bodies shows this is their only difference, so the /kk copy has simply drifted.
failure_scenario: A typo in a pair_coeff sub-style name produces a different (older) error message under hybrid/overlay/kk than under hybrid/overlay, and any future fix to the CPU coeff() will silently miss the KOKKOS copy.
suggested_fix: Sync the error message with src/pair_hybrid_overlay.cpp, or better, factor the shared logic so the KOKKOS overlay style does not duplicate coeff().
